articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Dynasty Cheat Sheet, Printable Rankings for Redraft Leagues
articles.summary: The dynasty-league portion of the fantasy football community is forever looking forward.
articles.body:
The dynasty-league portion of the fantasy football community is forever looking forward.

So, while they're awaiting the opening of the 2026 NFL season like everyone else, they're also thinking about a big picture that extends well beyond the upcoming campaign.

For long-term rebuilders, that might be their lone focus. But even win-right-now contenders should devote some roster space to long-term lottery tickets, because it's never a good thing to let the cupboard run dry.

To help get you prepped for this season but also stocked for the long haul, we're providing both dynasty and redraft rankings while spotlighting a few sleepers with clear dynasty-league appeal.

Douglas, a third-round rookie out of Texas Tech, already seems primed to play a major role in Miami's offense. There are targets available in this offense—which could often find itself playing from behind—and Douglas seems as likely as anyone to command them. He had a buzzy training camp, and if that gets him on the runway for a strong rookie season, he could be a dynasty asset for a while.

The now Mike McDaniel-led Chargers' offense feels like one you'll want exposure to, and Harris could be a sneaky-significant role in it. If nothing else, his blocking should keep him on the field, and that in turn should give him a chance to showcase his talents as a dynamic pass-catcher. He can dazzle both as a vertical field-spacer and a yards-after-catch creator.

Johnson looks better on film than he does on the workout circuit, which helps explain why he fell to this year's fifth round despite rushing for 1,451 yards and 12 touchdowns at Nebraska last season. The Chiefs clearly aren't complaining; they already cleared Johnson's path to playing time by waiving veteran Emari Demercado, and they could have passing-down duties ready for Johnson and maybe a lot more should Kenneth Walker III miss any time.

articles.title: Drake Maye Not Eyeing Revenge Game vs. Seahawks for Super Bowl 60 in Patriots' Season Opener
articles.summary: Drake Maye doesn't view the New England Patriots' season-opening clash with the Seattle Seahawks as an opportunity for revenge for the team's Super Bowl LX defeat.
articles.body:
Drake Maye doesn't view the New England Patriots' season-opening clash with the Seattle Seahawks as an opportunity for revenge for the team's Super Bowl LX defeat.

"They won the big one," Maye said Saturday, per MassLive's Mark Daniels .

Seattle was able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy by wrapping up a 29-13 win over New England in last season's Super Bowl matchup.

5 Fantasy Football League Winners for 2026 NFL Season

Buzz: Baker Frustrated with Bucs Talks 😠

Maye finished 27-of-43 for 295 yards and two touchdowns compared to two interceptions in the contest. He also lost a fumble.

It was a tough end to a promising overall season from the Patriots, as their deep playoff run came after a 2024 campaign in which they compiled a 4-13 record.

Maye was particularly stellar last year, finishing No. 2 in MVP voting and earning a Second Team All-Pro nod.

He completed 72.0 percent of his passes for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns while getting picked off just eight times. Maye's 77.1 QBR ranked No. 1 among 28 qualified quarterbacks, via ESPN .

The Patriots have their sights set on putting together another strong year in 2026 following a busy offseason. They made several additions on offense, signing wide receiver Romeo Doubs and guard Alijah Vera-Tucker in free agency.

They also acquired three-time Pro Bowl receiver A.J. Brown in a blockbuster trade with the Philadelphia Eagles on June 1.

Although the Seahawks didn't make any major external offseason additions and lost running back Kenneth Walker III in free agency, they're still a threat to win consecutive Super Bowl titles.

After all, they still boast an offense headlined by reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba and a defense that ranked No. 1 in the NFL by allowing a mere 17.2 points per game last season.

Even if a Patriots win over Seattle in Week 1 won't make up for their Super Bowl loss, it would help them open the year with plenty of momentum.

Kickoff between New England and Seattle is on Wednesday at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Tom Brady’s business venture reportedly faces $150 million debt as NFL legend remains committed to it ahead of the new season
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady, the New England Patriots’ legend, might have retired from the league but he has always been focused on his health and fitness. While he has.
articles.body: Tom Brady, the New England Patriots’ legend, might have retired from the league but he has always been focused on his health and fitness. While he has invested in a number of companies, one of his health tech investments suffered a major loss but it seems, Tom Brady is standing by it.Tom Brady works with his investment in Aescape after it reportedly suffered losses this yearA few hours ago, the seven time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady took to his social media to post about Aescape’s new launch. The company is an AI-powered robotic massage company he has invested in while also being its Chief Innovation Officer.In the clip, Tom Brady said, “Recovery was never optional for me. It’s why I could keep playing at 45. I didn’t want to just put my name on something — I wanted to help build it..I’m proud of what we’ve created together and excited for people to experience it this fall.”But the NFL legend’s post has raised eyebrows considering how Aescape went insolvent while facing over $150 million in debt earlier this year.As per reports, earlier this year, the company reportedly failed to keep up with high operating costs, capital expenditures and debt obligations.The company later brought in a new CEO Frank Britt who has reassured that Aescape Recovery (the company which owns Aescape’s technology) is perfectly functional.Back in May, in an interview with ATN, CEO Frank Britt said,“The arc of the narrative of somehow the company’s sort of out of business and bankrupt, it’s just preposterous…We are a company that is growing, we’re adding talent, we have a fortress balance sheet, the rate of growth of the use of the product with consumers is growing.”He added, “We’re hardly out of business…We’re quite the opposite.”Tom Brady has remained passionate about his fitness and often credits it for his success on the fieldInterestingly, Tom Brady has not commented on the drama yet as he is all set to headline this year’s opening session at the Eudemonia Summit in November in West Palm Beach, Florida, as he collaborates with Aescape.Last year, as he invested in Aescape, in an interview with CNBC Tom Brady also reflected on his fitness as he said, “After 23 years playing professionally, there’s no way I could have accomplished what I did professionally without all the massage work and recovery protocols…”The seven time Super Bowl champion added, “The reason why I’m still able to do what I love to do is because of the bodywork, the care that I received on a daily and weekly basis, and I want to try to make that available for everybody.”While Tom Brady is a multi millionaire, it seems he is pretty passionate about the companies he partners and invests in.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Somehow, the Miami Hurricanes have done it again with yet another Heisman-level quarterback
articles.summary: Darian Mensah's dominant debut at Miami continues a stunning pattern as Mario Cristobal lands yet another elite transfer portal quarterback.
articles.body: I remember it like it was yesterday. January 13, 2024. I was at a friend's birthday party with a group of fans representing each of the "Big 3" Florida schools (Miami, Florida, and Florida State). Being a Gator fan, I was relishing in joining my fellow Florida fanatics and Seminole supporters mocking the Miami contingent that they had whiffed on all their quarterback targets in the transfer portal. ACC SUPREMACY: IS IT REALLY THE MIAMI HURRICANES VERSUS THE FIELD FOR THE 2026 SEASON? As we laughed and reveled in their misery, a notification flashed across everyone's phone screen that changed the tide of the night in favor of the Canes fans. "BREAKING: Cam Ward, the ex-Washington State QB, heading to Miami." ONE OF THESE EIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS WILL BE HOISTING THE NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TROPHY IN 2026 The Hurricanes had found their guy, but after a Heisman-level season in 2024, their one year rental was off to the NFL Draft. So Miami's rivals fired up the trolls once again, and towards the end of the portal period, it looked like the Hurricanes were going to have to eat crow. That is, until they plucked Georgia quarterback Carson Beck from the ranks of the NFL Draft. Then the Canes rode another late transfer pickup to within a quarter of winning the national championship. So when Miami and Mario Cristobal were without a signal caller heading into the teeth of the offseason, we all knew better than to gloat. And that proved to be the right decision, as the Canes once again persuaded an NFL Draft hopeful - this time Duke transfer Darian Mensah - to hop in the boat in Coral Gables. UCLA QUARTERBACK ATTEMPTS TO EXPLOIT LOOPHOLE IN TRANSFER PORTAL WINDOW WITH UNIQUE TACTIC Mensah was given a king's ransom to make his way down to South Florida, and so far, though it's only been one game, that investment is looking to be paying dividends. I think I speak for the rest of college football when I ask: how do the Canes keep doing this? COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S AP TOP 25 IS OUT: WHO’S OVERRATED, UNDERRATED AND FLAT-OUT SNUBBED? I'm reminded of the famous scene from "Breaking Bad," when Aaron Paul's character screams "HE CAN'T KEEP GETTING AWAY WITH IT!" Granted, Miami played a Stanford team that was missing half its roster due to injury and probably isn't much to write home about even when fully healthy. But those numbers would look good in a 7-on-7 scrimmage, let alone in a conference game on the road three time zones from home. Mensah looked as good as the numbers suggested, too, ripping NFL-level throws and distributing the ball to his myriad playmakers, namely wide receiver Malachi Toney. Somehow, some way, Cristobal and the Canes have another quarterback who can realistically win the Heisman trophy and lead them on a deep Playoff run. The schedule for Miami won't offer a ton of resistance either; there will be far more Stanford-level teams than Playoff-caliber ones. When you combine all that and Mensah's skill with the weapons he's been surrounded with (not to mention elite offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson), the Hurricanes might be here to stay. If the offseason starts to drag on next January and they still haven't signed a quarterback, don't hit send on that X post with all the laughing emojis. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $145 million-plus in reported deals shows how he is building an empire beyond football
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is entering another NFL season with plenty of money already on the table, but his biggest financial story may be happening away from the .
articles.body: Travis Kelce is entering another NFL season with plenty of money already on the table, but his biggest financial story may be happening away from the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has secured a new contract while continuing to build interests in media, food, hospitality, sports and consumer brands. Together, those moves show how Kelce is turning his NFL fame into a business platform with a life beyond football.Travis Kelce's new Chiefs contract adds another layer to his wealthKelce's latest Chiefs deal gives him significant earning power for the 2026 season while leaving the door open for another year in Kansas City.The contract is structured as a three-year agreement, although the final two seasons contain important conditions. For 2026, Kelce is set to receive $12 million in guaranteed and roster-based compensation. That includes a $3 million base salary, a $3 million reporting bonus and $6 million in per-game roster bonuses.There is also as much as $3 million available through incentives. His potential earnings can rise if Kansas City reaches the playoffs and Kelce meets specific playing-time targets. Additional incentives are tied to reaching the Super Bowl.The structure gives Kelce and the Chiefs flexibility. A $40 million roster bonus tied to the 2028 season becomes fully guaranteed in June 2027, meaning the parties will have an important decision to make before then if he continues playing.For Kelce, however, football income is only one part of the picture.Travis Kelce investments stretch from Garage Beer to Six FlagsKelce's commercial reach has grown well beyond traditional endorsement deals. He reportedly earns around $30 million a year from endorsements, with major brands including Nike, State Farm, McDonald's, Pfizer, T-Mobile, Old Spice and Tide among his commercial partners.But ownership is where his strategy becomes more interesting.Kelce and his brother Jason became major investors in Garage Beer, a Cincinnati-based beer company, in 2024. Rather than simply attaching his name to the brand, Kelce has taken an active role in helping promote it. The company later reached a reported $200 million valuation after an investment from Durational Capital.His media business is another major asset. New Heights, the podcast he hosts with Jason, has developed into a standalone entertainment property. Amazon's Wondery signed the show to a reported deal worth more than $100 million for exclusive advertising sales and distribution.Kelce has also entered the restaurant business with Patrick Mahomes. The pair co-founded 1587 Prime in Kansas City with Noble 33, bringing their sports profiles into the hospitality world.Then came an even bigger corporate bet. In 2025, Kelce joined JANA Partners and other investors in taking an approximately 9% stake in Six Flags Entertainment. The investment was part of an activist strategy aimed at influencing the amusement park company's direction.His reported portfolio also includes Hydrow, Hilo Nutrition, Club Car Wash and an interest in the Alpine F1 Team. An earlier investment in Cholula Hot Sauce proved especially notable after McCormick acquired the brand for $800 million.The common thread is simple. Kelce is investing while his name still commands enormous attention. His new Chiefs contract keeps him on the field, while his business interests are building what could become an equally important legacy off it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I'll never stop being proud": Randi Mahomes gets emotional over Patrick Mahomes’ stunning 27-year full-circle moment in Times Square
articles.summary: NFL News: Randi Mahomes had a full-circle moment in New York City when she spotted her son Patrick Mahomes on a giant Times Square screen. Nearly three decades .
articles.body: Randi Mahomes had a full-circle moment in New York City when she spotted her son Patrick Mahomes on a giant Times Square screen. Nearly three decades after posing with her young son and her own mother, Randi returned to a very different picture of his life. This time, the boy beside her had become one of the NFL's biggest stars, making the moment especially meaningful for his proud mother.Randi Mahomes celebrates Patrick Mahomes' journey with a 27-year throwbackThe Kansas City Chiefs quarterback's rise has given his family plenty of milestones to celebrate, but Randi's latest post focused on something more personal than another football achievement.She shared two images side by side. The first showed Patrick as a child with Randi and his grandmother. The second showed Randi standing in Times Square in front of an advertisement featuring her son.The contrast between the photographs captured just how dramatically Patrick's life has changed. What began as a family photo 27 years ago eventually led to his face appearing on one of the world's most recognizable advertising landmarks.Randi summed up the emotion behind the moment in a short message:"27 years later and you ended up on one of the big screens," Randi wrote. "I'll never stop being proud of you."For Randi, Patrick's success also carries the memory of the years it took to get there. She has spoken openly about raising three children as a single mother and the demands that came with balancing work and family.Patrick Mahomes' NFL journey gives Randi Mahomes plenty to celebratePatrick entered the NFL in 2017, when the Chiefs selected him with the 10th overall pick. He quickly developed into the centerpiece of the franchise and has since won three Super Bowl titles and two NFL MVP awards.His path has not been without difficult stretches. The Chiefs missed the playoffs last season after finishing 6-11, ending a postseason run that had lasted for years. Patrick also suffered a torn ACL in December, forcing him into a long rehabilitation process.That makes Randi's Times Square post more than a celebration of fame. It is a reminder of the distance between Patrick's childhood and the career he has built.Randi has previously described the less visible side of raising her children while supporting Patrick's ambitions."People don't see the constant balancing act," Randi said. "You have to be the nurturer and the disciplinarian, the provider and the protector. You carry it all, and some days, that's heavier than anyone realizes."I missed a lot… school events, social outings, holidays. I worked long hours to make sure they had what they needed. That was the trade-off, but I'd do it again in a heartbeat."Now, with Patrick preparing for another season with Kansas City and working his way back from injury, Randi can look at that old family photograph and see how far her son has come.A child once standing beside his mother is now staring back from one of Times Square's giant screens. For Randi, 27 years made all the difference.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ reported $50,000 to $75,000 pay gap with NFL stars has fans demanding answers from Jerry Jones
articles.summary: NFL News: The Dallas Cowboys can command a multibillion-dollar valuation, but a growing debate is putting the spotlight on the people who help bring the franchi.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys can command a multibillion-dollar valuation, but a growing debate is putting the spotlight on the people who help bring the franchise’s image to life. Fans are questioning whether the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders receive enough compensation for their work, especially when compared with the enormous salaries earned by the team’s players and the value attached to the Cowboys brand.Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' reported pay sparks debateReports suggest Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders can earn as much as $2,500 per game, with total seasonal earnings estimated at roughly $50,000 to $75,000.Those numbers represent a major increase from the squad's previous reported pay scale. Yet the discussion is not simply about the hourly rate or the money earned on game day.Being a Cowboys Cheerleader involves far more than performing during NFL games. Members attend rehearsals, promotional appearances, community events and other obligations connected to the organization. The role can demand a substantial time commitment even though it is not structured like a traditional full-time NFL playing contract.Fox News highlighted the reported change in compensation, stating:“This will be year two of the ‘Boys cheerleaders making a reported 400% increase in salary compared to a previous salary scale. The new scale is said to pay $75/hr compared to $15/hour in previous years. While exact numbers aren’t public record, based on what cheerleaders have revealed via Netflix’s America’s Sweethearts series, experts believe the veteran cheerleaders can make $50k to $75k per season, including a rate of $2,500 per game based on the $75/hr. figure,” Fox News reported.The increase has therefore not gone unnoticed. Still, some fans believe the compensation should rise further.Cowboys fans want Jerry Jones to address cheerleaders' salariesThe discussion has gained momentum because of the enormous financial scale surrounding the Cowboys.Dallas is widely regarded as the world's most valuable sports franchise, with reports suggesting its potential valuation could exceed $20 billion. Against that backdrop, fans have questioned why the earnings of the cheerleaders remain relatively modest.The comparison becomes even sharper when placed alongside the contracts given to Cowboys players. Dak Prescott and other major stars have signed deals worth millions of dollars, reflecting the enormous revenue and commercial power of the NFL.Fans have now taken their concerns to social media, with some directly calling on Cowboys owner Jerry Jones to reconsider how the cheerleaders are compensated.The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are not a minor part of the franchise's public identity. Their performances, appearances and visibility have helped make the squad one of the best-known cheerleading teams in professional sports. Their popularity has also received renewed attention through Netflix's America’s Sweethearts, introducing the group to an even wider audience.That has made the salary debate harder to ignore.The central question for Cowboys fans is no longer simply how much a cheerleader earns per game. It is whether the compensation reflects the workload, visibility and commercial value attached to one of the NFL's most recognizable brands.For now, the reported pay scale shows that compensation has improved significantly. But the reaction from fans suggests many believe the conversation with Jerry Jones is far from over.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “Tom, come over, cutie": Alix Earle’s Tom Brady romance gets its biggest update yet as influencer breaks silence on Netflix reality show
articles.summary: NFL News: Alix Earle has finally offered her first public glimpse into the romance that had kept fans guessing for months. The 25-year-old influencer addressed .
articles.body: Alix Earle has finally offered her first public glimpse into the romance that had kept fans guessing for months. The 25-year-old influencer addressed her rumored relationship with Tom Brady on her new Netflix reality series, Earle Meets World. Rather than making a formal announcement, Earle kept things playful and vague, giving viewers just enough to understand that the two had grown closer.Alix Earle breaks her silence on Tom Brady relationshipThe moment came during the second episode of Earle Meets World, when Earle was rehearsing with her Dancing with the Stars partner Val Chmerkovskiy.His wife, Jenna Johnson, entered the studio and quickly picked up on the subject that had been following Earle in the headlines.When Johnson asked what was going on, Earle did not exactly confirm a relationship. Instead, she gave a coy response that suggested she was enjoying the new chapter of her life.“I don’t know what’s going on,” Earle responded. “I’m having fun.”Johnson then asked if the relationship was confirmed. Earle shrugged and again avoided putting a label on it.“No, I’m just having fun,” said Earle, coyly. “I know, a lot has changed since last time.”Johnson responded warmly before bringing up Earle's previous relationship with NFL player Braxton Berrios.“Love that for you,” Johnson replied. “How are you doing after, like, Braxton?”“I’m good,” replied Earle.Johnson then joked about Brady entering the picture, saying, “Then you were like, ‘Tom, come over, cutie,’ ” while pretending to make a phone call.The exchange gave viewers their clearest look yet at Earle's side of the story, even though neither she nor Brady has publicly defined the relationship.Tom Brady and Alix Earle's romance follows her difficult breakupRumors surrounding Earle and Brady began after they were seen together around New Year's Eve in St. Barths. The pair later crossed paths again during Super Bowl weekend, when social media footage showed them talking and dancing at a party.The speculation intensified after PEOPLE reported in February that a source described the pair as “hooking up.” Representatives for both Earle and Brady have not commented on the report.The timing also drew attention because Earle had recently ended her two-year relationship with Berrios. Their breakup came after a difficult period of long-distance dating, with Berrios focused on his NFL career and Earle working on Dancing with the Stars.Earle later spoke openly about how difficult the transition was for her. In a January TikTok, she admitted that being without a partner felt unfamiliar because she had spent much of her adult life in relationships.“I think I’ve just always had boyfriends. I was, like, a boyfriend hopper,” she said at the time. “This year, I’m gonna be dedicated to being OK with being alone. But I don’t know why I can’t do it. This is like growth or something, but I’m sad.”Earle also acknowledged that loneliness did not necessarily mean she was truly alone.“I feel like it just makes life feel so lonely, but it’s not, and I’m not lonely.”Now, with Earle Meets World giving audiences a closer look at her personal life, the Tom Brady chapter has moved from speculation into something she is willing to discuss, even if she is still keeping the details to herself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bloodied Josh Hoover delivers unforgettable four-touchdown debut for Indiana
articles.summary: The Hoosiers quarterback got banged up, but stayed around and picked up a big opening game.
articles.body:
Josh Hoover's first start for Indiana included four touchdown passes, a dominant victory and enough blood on his face mask to make the afternoon look far more difficult than it actually was.

That is one memorable way to begin a national championship defense.

Hoover completed 13 of 16 passes for 231 yards and four touchdowns as No. 6 Indiana overwhelmed North Texas 52-16 on Saturday in Bloomington. The former TCU quarterback entered the season with one of the most unenviable assignments in college football. He was replacing Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, who led Indiana through its historic championship campaign.

Hoover did not appear bothered by the expectations. His first pass in an Indiana uniform went for a 15-yard touchdown. He later connected with Charlie Becker for a 35-yard score immediately after North Texas had pulled within 24-13 early in the second half.

The response helped turn a potentially interesting game into another comfortable Indiana victory. Hoover also avoided committing a turnover, even after suffering a bloody nose that left his face mask noticeably covered in blood.

Indiana coach Curt Cignetti came away impressed with the composure his new quarterback displayed.

"I thought Josh was sharp," Cignetti said, according to The Associated Press . "I thought he played with a lot of confidence today." ( AP News )

Indiana may have found another perfect fit at quarterback

Nobody should confuse North Texas with the challenges Indiana will face later in the season. Still, Hoover's efficiency was exactly what the Hoosiers needed to see.

He did not force throws or attempt to recreate Mendoza's championship season by himself. Hoover distributed the ball to Indiana's playmakers and allowed the offense to operate around him.

Becker caught four passes for 64 yards and two touchdowns. Nick Marsh and Davion Chandler also caught scoring passes, while Boston College transfer Turbo Richard rushed for two touchdowns.

Indiana extended the longest active winning streak in the FBS to 17 games. The Hoosiers have also won 16 consecutive games at home.

Those streaks bring increased expectations, but Cignetti's program has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to replace important players without losing its identity.

Hoover's arrival may be the latest example.

One performance cannot answer every question about Indiana's championship defense. It can, however, establish that the moment is not too large for the new quarterback.

Hoover took a hit, played through a bloody nose and kept delivering touchdowns. For an Indiana team attempting to prove last season was the start of something sustainable, that was an ideal opening statement.

At the end of the day, Indiana lost a Heisman Trophy quarterback, but Hoover's gritty debut showed the Hoosiers may not have lost their championship edge.

articles.title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers hopes to be 'supporting my pregnant wife' by next year after final NFL season
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers told Mad Dog Sports Radio he hopes to have a pregnant wife by next year as he prepares for life after what may be his final season.
articles.body: Next Sunday will mark the beginning of what could be Aaron Rodgers’ final NFL season. The four-time league MVP signed a one-year contract during the offseason to return to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Rodgers’ potential retirement has been widely discussed, and more details emerged this week about what his life could look like beyond football. Starting a family appears to be among the 42-year-old quarterback’s priorities whenever he does decide to step away from the game. Rodgers told SiriusXM that he hopes he and his wife will be in the midst of doing so by this time next year. STEELERS LEGEND JEROME BETTIS SAYS THERE'S 'EXCITEMENT IN THE AIR' AS AARON RODGERS RETURNS FOR FINAL SEASON "I'm hopefully going to be supporting my pregnant wife because we're going to start a family and I am not going to be making a lot of appearances or statements," Rodgers told SiriusXM's "Mad Dog Radio." "And I’m looking forward to a life of quiet after 22 years in the pros and three in college and getting my body healed up and working on a family. That’s what I’m looking forward to." The conversation then turned to whether Rodgers was simply looking ahead or hinting at something more immediate. "I’m talking about I’m hoping that I have a pregnant wife by next [year] this time," Rodgers said. After a period of distance from some relatives, Rodgers acknowledged that reconnecting with them had influenced his hopes of starting a family. Rodgers added that he's enjoyed spending time with his brother’s children. AARON RODGERS CREDITS WIFE FOR FAMILY REUNION AFTER MORE THAN A DECADE OF ESTRANGEMENT "I'm definitely excited about it," Rodgers said. "I mean, being back in my family's lives, I'm having a lot of fun being Uncle Aaron. I have a few godkids that I'm involved with, but being Uncle Aaron to my brother's kids has been a lot of fun." "And the more I'm around them, the more I get excited, and so does the wife, about having some of our own," he continued. "So, I'm excited for that. I can't wait for that next chapter of life and all that that entails, and sleepless nights and crying babies and changing diapers and all those things, I'm looking forward to all of it." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Since announcing his marriage, Rodgers has kept his wife’s personal life out of the spotlight. The NFL star has described his spouse as a "private person."

articles.title: Could Tony Romo’s $72M CBS deal be in jeopardy? Analyst makes ominous 95% prediction after former NFL star’s arrest
articles.summary: NFL News: Tony Romo’s future with CBS looks increasingly uncertain after his July arrest in Wisconsin. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback remains on leave, w.
articles.body: Tony Romo’s future with CBS looks increasingly uncertain after his July arrest in Wisconsin. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback remains on leave, while J.J. Watt has stepped into his spot alongside Jim Nantz on the network’s lead NFL crew.Now, sports media insider John Ourand has offered a grim prediction. He believes Romo has only a slim chance of returning, even though CBS has not officially made a final decision on his future. John Ourand puts Tony Romo’s CBS return at just 5 percentOurand gave his assessment during an appearance on Puck’s “The Powers That Be Daily” podcast. He believes there is a 95 percent chance Romo will not return to CBS.“I think it’s highly unlikely,” Ourand said on the podcast. “And by highly unlikely, I think it’s like 95 percent that he’s not back at CBS.”The prediction comes after CBS placed Romo on leave following his July arrest in Wisconsin. The network then turned to J.J. Watt, who joined Nantz and Tracy Wolfson for its top NFL broadcast team.That move gives CBS a ready-made alternative while the network weighs Romo’s future. More importantly, CBS has made it clear that the issue goes beyond what happens in court.CBS Sports president David Berson said in August that there was “no timetable or final decision” regarding Romo. He also said the network had to consider the “impact on our image and on our brand.”That comment matters because the arrest footage has continued to draw attention, creating another concern for CBS if Romo returns to its biggest NFL broadcasts.Ourand also pointed to the 44-minute body-camera video as a potential problem. He said on the September 4 podcast that whenever Romo says or does something unusual in the booth, the footage could bring fresh jokes and memes about whether he had been drinking. Tony Romo’s $180 million CBS deal could make the exit complicatedRomo’s contract adds another layer to the situation. He signed a 10-year, $180 million deal with CBS in 2020, meaning roughly four years and $72 million remain.Ourand believes CBS could see an opportunity to save money, but he expects negotiations if the network decides to part ways with Romo.“The question is: What is the number that would make Tony Romo sort of walk away without a fight?” Ourand said on the podcast.Romo, meanwhile, has made his own position clear. In an Instagram statement on September 1, he accepted responsibility for his actions, discussed his struggles with pain medication and alcohol, and said he hopes to return to CBS.So, while CBS has not closed the door publicly, Watt now gives the network another option. Unless that experiment falls apart, Ourand sees Romo’s return as highly unlikely.Still, the financial side cannot disappear from the conversation. With roughly $72 million reportedly remaining on Romo’s CBS deal, any decision to move on could lead to serious negotiations between the two sides. For CBS, the question is no longer just whether Romo returns, but how much it may cost if he does not.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Steelers Recent Practice Squad Signing-Handed Punishment From NFL
articles.summary: The NFL handed a recently signed Pittsburgh Steelers practice squad player a punishment for actions in the last preseason game. The post Steelers Recent Prac...
articles.body:
The NFL preseason came to an end on the last weekend of August. Although none of the scores or records count in the standings or record books, the NFL still tracks a few things.

NFL Fined Steelers Defensive Back Doneiko Slaughter

One thing the NFL takes seriously in the preseason is unsportsmanlike penalties, and the NFL fined Pittsburgh Steelers defensive back Doneiko Slaughter.

The NFL fined Slaughter $4,917 for an unsportsmanlike conduct taunting penalty in the second quarter of the Steelers' third preseason game against the Buffalo Bills.

Slaughter was the only Steelers player the NFL fined during their three preseason games.

The Steelers signed Slaughter to a reserve futures deal this past winter after the Jacksonville Jaguars signed him as an undrafted free agent following the 2025 NFL Draft.

However, Slaughter did not make the Steelers' 53-man roster as they waived him on Sunday. But Pittsburgh added him to its practice squad.

Slaughter played five seasons of college football, starting his career at Tennessee, where he appeared in 43 games for the Volunteers from 2020 to 2023. He recorded 66 solo tackles, 21 assisted tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss, three sacks and one interception. Slaughter then transferred to another SEC school for his last season of college football, heading down to Arkansas in 2025. He appeared in 12 games, recording 44 solo tackles, 36 assisted tackles, three tackles for loss and one sack.

Pittsburgh Will Face a Coach It Has Seen for the Last Six Seasons in Week 1

The Steelers have a week before they take on the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET. Many Pittsburgh fans will know who is on the other side.

Atlanta hired a new head coach this season: Kevin Stefanski. Stefanski coached one of the Steelers' biggest rivals, the Cleveland Browns , for the last six seasons.

Stefanski has a 6-6 record as a head coach against the Steelers, and he even helped beat Pittsburgh in the 2020-21 Wild Card round, but he wasn't on the sidelines.

Since the 2020 season was the COVID season, Stefanski came down with COVID right before the playoff game, and he had to stay home and watch from his basement.

Special teams coordinator Mike Priefer was the interim head coach for the game and helped the Browns win 48-37 in Pittsburgh.

The Browns fired Stefanski this offseason after finishing 5-12, and he is now looking to get back on track with his second stint as an NFL head coach.

Pittsburgh also has a new head coach, Mike McCarthy. Stefanski has a 1-1 record against McCarthy. McCarthy lost to Stefanski when he was the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys in 2020, but went to Cleveland and defeated them in Week 1 of the 2024 season.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns news: The final Sunday before the Browns return
articles.summary: The latest Cleveland Browns news and notes from around the NFL in the September 6 edition of the Sunday Dawg Chow.
articles.body:
We have reached the final Sunday before the 2026 NFL regular season begins on Wednesday night when the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots.

Thursday brings the Los Angeles Rams (who have a new defensive player, in case you had not heard) and the San Francisco 49ers from Melbourne, Australia.

Then, next Sunday, the game that everyone has been waiting for as the Cleveland Browns take the field for their first regular-season game under head coach Todd Monken. The unlucky opponent? The Jacksonville Jaguars.

That is still a few days away, so have a great holiday weekend, and let's kick off the day with the latest edition of the Sunday Dawg Chow.

Browns 2026 season: 5 reasons I'm excited, 3 reasons I'm concerned (Jared Mueller) – "While we are ready to move forward with Cleveland's 2026 season, the decisions made this offseason undergird everyone's expectations. Here is a list of a few things I'm excited about and concerned about.

Based on 2025, Browns will need at least this many passing yards to make the playoffs (Jared Mueller) – "There are so many unknowns about the Cleveland Browns going into next week's season opener. How will HC Todd Monken do in the role for the first time at the NFL level? What will the downturn from Myles Garrett to Jared Verse do to the defense? How will all the young roster players look in real games with fewer veterans around them?"

Is the 5,000-yard QB extinct? Where Browns find themselves in the NFL's cyclical nature (Jared Mueller) – "The NFL has been a "head coach, offensive play caller, and quarterback league" for a while now. The Cleveland Browns hope they have the first two locked up with HC Todd Monken, but few believe that Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, or Taylen Green fit the mold of a franchise-level quarterback."

Share your thoughts in Dawgs By Nature's Feed in the comment section or by following this link to the Feed post .

Spencer Fano's climb to No. 9 pick started with dad-demanded footwork drills when he was 6 (Browns Zone) – "Agility ladders are common on a football practice field. They are placed on the ground, and the players — primarily running backs and receivers but even linemen on occasion — run through them to improve footwork and quickness. The ladder is unusual for a backyard. Especially one used by a 6-year-old."

Browns rookie KC Concepcion might be Todd Monken's most dangerous weapon this season (cleveland.com) – "The easiest way to improve an offense is to find players who can create yards without requiring everything around them to be perfect. For the Browns, rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion has already demonstrated that kind of ability. The first-round pick can contribute as a receiver, runner and punt returner, giving head coach Todd Monken a versatile weapon who can affect all three phases of the game."

Browns hoping improved health can lift defensive line entering opener (Beacon Journal) – "The injury bug bit the Browns in multiple areas during the course of training camp. The area most impacted was their defensive line."

Exclusive Interview with Adin Huntington (Cleveland Browns YouTube) – "Nathan Zegura sits down with Adin Huntington to talk going into year 2, what gives him drive, and moving up to becoming a starter."

Will Kyler Murray end the Vikings' tragicomic QB history? (ESPN) – "Long before he signed with the Minnesota Vikings this spring, Kyler Murray understood the tragicomic nature of their attempt to find a stable long-term quarterback."

Jayden Daniels is ready for a new offense. His first task: Learn how to huddle (The Athletic) – "Dan Quinn and the Washington Commanders' coaching staff were watching video footage from a GoPro affixed to Jayden Daniels' helmet, hoping to see how he went through his progressions, when they found something else."

Giants' Greg Newsome on facing George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb in Week 1: 'Great players, but I like our chances' (NFL.com) – "The extended window before the start of the 2026 NFL season provides opportunity for a little extra bulletin board material. New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II, as complimentary as he was while doing so, might have provided some for the Dallas Cowboys ahead of their prime-time Week 1 matchup."

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

articles.title: New Angels Owner Stan Kroenke Has Already Made Nearly $20 Billion On His Sports Teams
articles.summary: After conquering every other major American men’s pro league, the billionaire behind the Avalanche, Nuggets and Rams is vying for one more win, on and off th...
articles.body:
Major pro sports teams have turned dozens of franchise owners into billionaires many times over in the last quarter-century, but nobody has made as much money from sports ownership as Stan Kroenke.

The reclusive billionaire—who announced on Tuesday that he is buying a majority stake in the Los Angeles Angels from Arte Moreno , at a valuation of roughly $4 billion, according to a person with knowledge of the deal—made his fortune in real estate and stands as America's largest private landowner, with some 2.7 million acres of ranches. But it is his sports team investments from the last three decades that now make up the majority of his estimated $27.6 billion net worth . Even before the Angels deal is complete, Kroenke's stakes in the NFL's Los Angeles Rams, the NBA's Denver Nuggets, the NHL's Colorado Avalanche, MLS's Colorado Rapids, the Premier League's Arsenal FC and the Women's Super League's Arsenal WFC are worth around $22 billion net of debt, according to Forbes estimates.

Better yet, the 79-year-old Kroenke acquired those half-dozen teams for around $2.4 billion (or about $3.8 billion adjusted for inflation). By comparison, the Rams, who have posted an 18.9% compound annual growth rate since 2010 to outpace the NFL average by five percentage points and easily beat the S&P 500 index's 12.7% annualized return over the same period, were worth $10.5 billion on their own last year, according to Forbes estimates, making them the third-most-valuable sports team in the world.

The man who has earned the nickname "Silent Stan" may not ever crow about it, but when his MLB purchase closes, Kroenke will also be unmatched among sports owners in terms of breadth, becoming the first person ever to control teams in each of North America's five major men's professional leagues.

Kroenke's portfolio has benefited from the run-up in team prices across the U.S. sports landscape—MLB valuations have more than doubled on average over the past decade, and each of the other four major North American leagues have seen their average valuations rise at least threefold, driven by surging media rights fees, the modernization of stadiums and investors' insatiable appetite for an asset that remains fundamentally scarce. (Even after the recent additions of expansion teams in MLS, there are just 154 franchises across the five major American men's leagues.)

But Kroenke's clubs have done their part, too. The Rams, for instance, have gone from No. 28 in the NFL in revenue the year before his purchase, when they were still based in St. Louis, to No. 3 in the league in Los Angeles, generating an estimated $764 million in 2024. That translated to operating income of $244 million that season, tying them for third among the world's most profitable sports teams in Forbes' 2026 ranking.

The clubs' on-field performance has been even more impressive. The Rams won Super Bowl LVI in 2022 at their new home of SoFi Stadium, the Avalanche won the Stanley Cup the same year, and the Nuggets took home the NBA title in 2023. Meanwhile, in May, Arsenal won the Premier League for the first time in 22 years, and its women's club won the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup in February.

That track record hasn't always been enough to win over fans. Arsenal supporters continued to grumble about Kroenke's ownership long after he acquired a majority stake in the club in 2011, launching a "Kroenke Out" protest in 2021 after the team flirted with European soccer's doomed Super League proposal , and he remains reviled in St. Louis after moving the Rams to California in 2016. But after 11 straight losing seasons on Moreno's watch, and a total of one playoff series in the past 16 years, the Angels faithful chose to celebrate the news of Kroenke's purchase agreement this week.

"He is competitive, he demands excellence, and he's not a person who needs the adulation of the fans," says Marc Ganis, president of consulting firm Sportscorp, who has known Kroenke for more than 30 years. "He doesn't get too high or too low based on what the sports talk radio guys are saying today or may say tomorrow."

In some respects, an MLB deal represents a return to Kroenke's roots. His full name is Enos Stanley Kroenke—after St. Louis Cardinals Hall of Famers Enos Slaughter and Stan Musial, who led the team to a World Series title the year before Kroenke's birth—and he grew up listening to Cardinals games on the radio with his father and grandfather in the tiny town of Mora, Missouri.

Kroenke went on to earn an undergraduate degree and an M.B.A. from the University of Missouri and made his first fortune in real estate after marrying Walmart heir Ann Walton (who separately has a $14.1 billion net worth , according to Forbes estimates). Kroenke made a habit of developing large plots of land into active shopping centers, often anchored by a Walmart, and today he owns around 60 million square feet of commercial real estate, in addition to the ranchland he owns in states including Texas, New Mexico, Nevada and Wyoming.

That real estate savvy would serve Kroenke well in his second act as a sports owner. He now controls the Rams' SoFi Stadium, Arsenal's Emirates Stadium and Ball Arena, the home of the Nuggets, the Avalanche and the National Lacrosse League's Colorado Mammoth (also owned by Kroenke).

"Stan's first love is real estate development. He's very meticulous when it comes to real estate, very hands-on, and he's done extraordinarily well with it," says Sportscorp's Ganis. "Wherever you see Stan getting involved in sports, you should always think that there's a real estate component."

After a failed bid to bring an NFL expansion team to his home state in 1993, Kroenke bought 30% of the then-Los Angeles Rams in 1995 to facilitate their move to St. Louis, and he added another 10% two years later, paying a reported $80 million in total for his 40% stake.

In 1999, around the time it was being acquired by Liberty Media, Ascent Entertainment Group was looking to unload its sports assets: the Nuggets, the Avalanche and their new arena, then called the Pepsi Center. A $400 million deal with another Walton—Ann's sister, Nancy Walton Laurie , and her husband, Bill Laurie—fell through because of a shareholder lawsuit, and the city of Denver rejected billionaire telecom investor Donald Sturm's subsequent $461 million bid because he wouldn't commit to keeping the teams there. Kroenke swooped in with a $450 million agreement in 2000.

That year, Forbes valued the Nuggets at $175 million and the Avalanche at $198 million; those values had climbed to $4.6 billion and $1.95 billion, respectively, by 2025, ranking the teams No. 17 in the NBA and No. 18 in the NHL .

In 2003, Kroenke acquired Major League Soccer's Colorado Rapids for an undisclosed price at a time when the league's viability was still in doubt—today, the Rapids are worth $450 million, No. 28 in MLS . He also launched Altitude Sports & Entertainment in 2004 as a regional sports network to broadcast his teams' games in the Denver area.

When Rams majority owner Georgia Frontiere died in 2008 and her children put the team up for sale, Kroenke had first dibs, with an option to match any external bids, and he wound up buying the rest of the club in 2010, spending $450 million to value the franchise at $750 million.

In the years that followed, as he played hardball with the city, St. Louis put together a proposal to renovate the Rams' outdated Edward Jones Dome, but Kroenke ultimately opted out of the lease to build a gleaming $5 billion football palace and surrounding development called Hollywood Park on roughly 300 acres of land he had acquired in Inglewood, California. The Rams then headed west for the 2016 season, reportedly paying a $645 million relocation fee that was split among other NFL teams.

The city of St. Louis sued Kroenke and the NFL, alleging that he had violated the league's relocation guidelines, and in 2021, the parties settled for $790 million, with Kroenke reportedly footing $571 million of that bill.

Much to Missourians' chagrin, the move has been a resounding success for the Rams' business, catapulting their team value from an estimated $1.45 billion in their last year in St. Louis in 2015 to $10.5 billion in 2025, No. 2 in the NFL. Meanwhile, the franchise has become a perennial contender, reaching the Super Bowl twice in the past eight years and drawing the nod from oddsmakers as the favorite to hoist the Lombardi Trophy this season.

Now, with his son Josh acting as governor of the Nuggets and Avalanche and taking the reins as heir apparent to his Kroenke Sports & Entertainment empire, Kroenke is laying the groundwork to develop 55 acres surrounding Ball Arena in Denver with residential buildings, a hotel and a concert venue. It wouldn't be surprising if part of his plan with the Angels is to modernize the team's 60-year-old stadium and reimagine the surrounding area as well.

Fans in Anaheim certainly wouldn't mind a similar playbook if it brings them a taste of the Rams' recent success.

articles.title: Will Commanders' defender win another rookie of the year award in 2026?
articles.summary: Sonny Styles is a leading contender to win NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2026.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have had an NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year (Jayden Daniels, 2024) and an NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year (Chase Young, 2020) in the last six years. Could Washington add another award-winning rookie in 2026?

Linebacker Sonny Styles enters the NFL with plenty of fanfare this season. The No. 7 overall pick out of Ohio State is coming off an All-American season and one of the best individual NFL combine performances in years. He played in Washington's first two preseason games, but not enough for fans to see his full potential. That was by design.

As part of their 2026 season preview , ESPN recently looked at the rookie class, with analysts making predictions on who would win the offensive and defensive rookie of the year awards.

Styles was the pick for the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year.

It's how Washington plans to use Styles that makes his case intriguing. The Commanders will want to take advantage of his ability on blitzes after Styles generated pressure on 20% of his blitz opportunities at Ohio State. He also had the lowest missed-tackle rate among linebackers in this draft class. That gives the No. 7 pick multiple ways to build a DROY résumé: tackles, sacks and impact plays.

ESPN predicted that Styles would finish with 129 tackles as a rookie in 2026.

Styles' former college teammate Arvell Reese came in at No. 2, while Bears safety Dillon Thieneman was No. 3. Surprisingly, Styles' other former college teammate, safety Caleb Downs, wasn't among the top five. That seems hard to believe, as Downs is expected to have a big rookie season for the Cowboys.

So, can Styles become Washington's latest rookie of the year? The Commanders open the 2026 season next Sunday at Philadelphia.

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick on his political evolution and which current politician he believes is ‘moving the needle’
articles.summary: Colin Kaepernick praised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as a politician he finds inspiring, 10 years after the former quarterback famously said he wouldn’t vote in the presidential election because he didn’t want to support “the system of oppression.”
articles.body: Colin Kaepernick praised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as a politician he finds inspiring, 10 years after the former quarterback famously said he wouldn’t vote in the presidential election because he didn’t want to support “the system of oppression.” Kaepernick made the comments during an extensive interview with NBC News in which he discussed his political evolution. In 2016, the same year he began taking a knee to protest police brutality against Black people, Kaepernick created a firestorm when he revealed he didn’t vote in the presidential election between Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump. Kaepernick was critical of both candidates, describing them as “proven liars.” He decried Trump as “openly racist” and also criticized Clinton for her use of the term “super predators” when defending the 1994 crime bill signed by her husband, President Bill Clinton. “You know, I think it would be hypocritical of me to vote,” Kaepernick told reporters following Trump’s first election in November 2016. “I said from the beginning I was against oppression, I was against the system of oppression. I’m not going to show support for that system. And to me, the oppressor isn’t going to allow you to vote your way out of your oppression.” Kaepernick writes in his new memoir, “The Perilous Fight,” that he has since amended his stance on voting, particularly after the fallout from Trump’s first term. “The realization coming out of the 2016 election is how significant the implications can be of not voting, even if you don’t fully think this candidate represents you, and I’ve seen that,” Kaepernick told NBC News. “We’ve seen it with the Supreme Court. We’ve seen it with federal judges.” “Part of trying to seek the best way for us to move forward and have impact is also realizing the moments where the intention of the perspective was right, but the strategy behind it actually wasn’t,” he added. Kaepernick writes in his book that he voted for the Democratic candidates in the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections and that he now recognizes that not participating in electoral politics was “irresponsible.” As far as current-day politicians he finds inspiring, Kaepernick mentioned Mamdani, the 34-year-old democratic socialist who has become one of the most recognizable names in politics. “When we talk about leaders that are moving the needle right now, I think we’re seeing real impact coming out of Mamdani,” Kaepernick said. “It is very refreshing for a lot of people to see someone in a political role saying, ‘I am prioritizing the people’s needs. I’m going to hold people accountable to that, and we are just going to execute and deliver on this over and over again.’” Mamdani was elected in November 2025, running on an ambitious platform that included expanding universal childcare, freezing the rent in rent-stabilized apartments and opening city-run grocery stores. In an early-August poll by Siena, 69% of New Yorkers had a favorable view of the mayor. Kaepernick added that Mamdani’s style of governance could inspire more people to be politically engaged. “Ultimately, I think a lot of those people who are out there that say, ‘Hey, this doesn’t represent me, I’m not voting, or I don’t feel great about the politicians out there,’ it’s because they aren’t seeing people move in that way. The more that we see that come, we’ll see more and more people involved and excited about what is happening in the political sphere.”

images.caption: NFL Quarterback and Activist Colin Kaepernick has his portrait taken at the Chrysler Building in New York City on July 30, 2026.
